title: International WASH & climate-resilience grants — next intake / waitlist
status: 2026 deadline passed; applications after June 30 placed on waitlist
geography: Selected countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America
eligible: Potentially — nonprofit eligibility plus new-partner reference requirement
reason: Canadian foundation with an explicit Water and Sanitation action area, grants up to $35,000, and a country list that overlaps heavily with WaterAid. The 2026 normal deadline has passed, so the best action is to prepare for the next cycle or ask about the waitlist.
next_action: Map a small, locally led WASH project to Roncalli criteria; verify next intake timing and identify a reference organization if WaterAid is treated as a new partner.
evidence: Roncalli funds 100+ Global South projects yearly; Water and Sanitation is an explicit action area; grants may be up to CAD 35,000; 2026 applications after June 30 go to a waitlist.

evidence_items.quote: Applications received after June 30, 2026 will be placed on a waiting list; projects must meet criteria and take place in a country where the Foundation works.
Water and Sanitation projects may include wells, pumps, reservoirs, latrines, handwashing stations, awareness and training.

title: International Development — maternal & child health / women & girls
status: 2026 EOI window closed; monitor next cycle
amount: Recent grants roughly CAD 20,000–250,000; varies by cycle
eligible: Registered Canadian charities can be eligible; verify next call
reason: The Foundation explicitly funds international development, has supported WASH-related work in Nigeria and Ethiopia, and its program guidance has linked WASH infrastructure to maternal and child health. The current 2026 EOI window is closed.
next_action: Add to Funding Watch and prepare a next-cycle case around WASH + maternal/child health or women and girls in a WaterAid priority country.
evidence: The International Development program supports women and girls, primarily in Sub-Saharan Africa; the 2026 EOI window closed July 13 and is under review.

evidence_items.quote: International Development focuses on Maternal & Child Health and Women & Girls Opportunity, with a primary focus on Sub-Saharan Africa; 2026 EOI window closed July 13.
Recent recipients include Lifewater Canada for clean water and sanitation in Nigeria and Operation Eyesight Canada for integrated WASH and maternal/child health in Ethiopia.

title: Unsolicited proposal pathway for international assistance
status: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
eligible: Canadian NGOs and private-sector organizations may submit if requirements are met
reason: GAC is an established WaterAid Canada funder and accepts unsolicited proposals on an ongoing basis for ODA-eligible countries. This is strategically important but should be pursued only when a strong concept aligns with GAC priorities and WaterAid capacity.
next_action: Develop a concept around one or more WaterAid target countries and confirm fit against current GAC policy priorities before entering Partners@International.
evidence: GAC lists unsolicited proposals as ongoing for all ODA-eligible countries and non-governmental/private-sector organizations.

title: Canadian Climate Partnerships Initiative
eligible: No — only specifically invited organizations can apply; WaterAid Canada is not on the published invitee list
reason: Strong geographic and climate-resilience fit, but the call is invitation-only and WaterAid Canada is not among the published invitees. This is exactly the kind of attractive-looking opportunity the system should reject early.
next_action: Do not spend proposal hours on this call. Monitor future GAC climate-finance opportunities and partnership routes.
evidence: The call is invitation-only and publishes the invited organizations; WaterAid Canada is not listed.

title: Nexa Lighthouse — Asia and Pacific climate-health innovation
eligible: Potentially, but thematic fit is narrower than WASH
reason: Canadian global-health funder with an open Asia/Pacific climate-health opportunity, but the current call focuses on mosquito-borne infections, extreme heat and air quality rather than WASH. It is relevant only if WaterAid has a genuinely aligned innovation.
next_action: Review the full Nexa call for a defensible WASH-to-climate-health innovation fit; decline if the concept would stretch beyond the stated drivers.
evidence: GCC lists Nexa Lighthouse Asia/Pacific as open to Nov. 17, 2026 for climate-health risk innovations.

title: Global South research & innovation funding — monitor for WASH/climate calls
status: No open calls shown on funding page at current check
eligible: Call-specific; Canadian organizations require legal entity and CRA number
reason: IDRC is a Canadian Crown corporation funding research and innovation in developing regions. It is more research-oriented than standard WASH delivery funding, but can be highly relevant for evidence, climate resilience, health systems and research partnerships.
next_action: Subscribe to IDRC funding alerts and tag future calls that include water security, climate resilience, global health or eligible WaterAid countries.
evidence: IDRC funds research and innovation in developing regions; the funding page currently shows no open calls and offers funding alerts.

title: Young Africa Works / health & livelihoods partnership prospect
status: Partnership development; no general open grant call identified
eligible: Partnership model — not a standard open grant application
reason: The Foundation is a registered Canadian charity with deep program presence in several WaterAid countries. WASH is not its core focus, so this is a strategic partnership prospect where WaterAid can connect WASH, health systems, women and youth livelihoods rather than a direct WASH grant call.
next_action: Build a partnership thesis for health workforce or WASH-linked youth livelihoods in one of the Foundation’s African country programs; do not treat as an open call.
evidence: Mastercard Foundation is a registered Canadian charity with offices and programs across multiple African countries, focused on youth employment, education and financial inclusion.

title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives — country-level calls
status: Country calls vary; many 2026 calls closed — monitor next cycle
eligible: Primarily local organizations; country offices/local partners may be eligible depending on call
reason: CFLI is a Canadian government funding mechanism implemented through embassies/high commissions. It is most useful for WaterAid country offices or local partners rather than WaterAid Canada directly, making it a partnership and local-delivery pathway.
next_action: For each WaterAid country, monitor the relevant Canadian mission’s CFLI call and assess whether the local WaterAid entity or partner is eligible.
evidence: CFLI funds small high-impact projects in 120+ ODA-eligible countries; local organizations plan and implement projects and Canadian missions select them.
applicant_types: other eligible entities per country call

title: Donor-advised-fund cultivation channel for WaterAid Canada
status: Active relationship channel; no unsolicited applications
geography: WaterAid Canada can receive grants as a Canadian registered charity; funds can support its global mission subject to donor/fund designation
eligible: Yes as a Canadian registered charity; donor recommendation required
reason: Aqueduct was a named WaterAid Canada foundation supporter in 2020/21 and grants to Canadian registered charities, but it has no open public application program. This is a donor-relationship prospect rather than a cold grant application.
next_action: Map existing or prospective WaterAid supporters who use Aqueduct donor-advised funds; do not submit an unsolicited grant request.
evidence: Aqueduct grants to Canadian registered charities but does not accept unsolicited applications; WaterAid Canada previously listed Aqueduct Foundation among transformational foundation supporters.

evidence_items.quote: Aqueduct makes grants to Canadian registered charities and qualified donees; grants are generally made at the recommendation of donors and grant advisors and there is no open public granting program.
WaterAid Canada listed Aqueduct Foundation among foundations making transformational gifts in 2020/21.

title: Donor-advised-fund cultivation channel for WaterAid Canada
status: Active DAF platform; donor recommendation required
geography: WaterAid Canada is a Canadian registered charity eligible to receive Benefaction grants
eligible: Yes as a registered Canadian charity; access depends on donor recommendation
reason: Benefaction was a named WaterAid Canada foundation supporter in 2020/21. Its primary grantmaking follows recommendations from donor-advised funds, so the opportunity is relationship cultivation rather than an open call.
next_action: Identify WaterAid major-donor and advisor relationships connected to Benefaction funds and prepare a concise case for support tied to priority WaterAid countries.
evidence: Benefaction grants to registered Canadian charities and qualified donees and WaterAid Canada has previously named Benefaction as a supporter.

evidence_items.quote: Benefaction restricts granting to registered Canadian charities and other permitted qualified donees; its donor-advised funds recommend grants.
WaterAid Canada listed Benefaction Foundation among foundations making transformational gifts in 2020/21.

title: Invitation-only international-development cultivation prospect
amount: Varies; current portfolio should be reviewed
geography: Canadian foundation with selected international-development and human-rights grants
location: Potentially multiple WaterAid countries through Canadian-charity programming
reason: Donner was a named WaterAid Canada supporter in 2020/21 and still makes some international-development grants, but its grantmaking is invitation-only and current strategic fit must be confirmed.
next_action: Review WaterAid’s prior Donner relationship and current contacts; approach only through an appropriate relationship path rather than an unsolicited application.
evidence: Donner states its granting is invitation-only. Its current grants include some international-development and human-rights support.

evidence_items.quote: The Donner Canadian Foundation’s granting is by invitation-only; staff do not regularly respond to unsolicited requests.
WaterAid Canada listed Donner Canadian Foundation among foundations making transformational gifts in 2020/21.

title: International WASH partnership cultivation
status: Partnership / co-design; no unsolicited project proposals
geography: International WASH projects including multiple WaterAid countries
location: Colombia, India, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Burkina Faso and other international geographies
eligible: Partnership fit is strong; One Drop does not accept project proposals
reason: One Drop is a Canadian WASH foundation with direct historic partnership with WaterAid Canada in Mali and active or completed work across several WaterAid countries. Access is partnership-based, not an open grant call.
next_action: Use the prior WaterAid–One Drop partnership as the relationship entry point and explore co-designed financing for a priority country rather than sending a cold proposal.
evidence: One Drop works with financial partners and international NGOs but says it does not accept project proposals; WaterAid Canada partnered with One Drop on Mali: Healthy Communities.

evidence_items.quote: One Drop works with financial partners and international NGOs to implement WASH projects and does not accept project proposals; projects are co-designed.
WaterAid Canada states Mali: Healthy Communities was delivered in partnership with the One Drop Foundation.
